findings.title: `LaunchTracker.confirm` is dead in production code and duplicated by direct mutation
findings.description: `LaunchTracker.confirm()` has no caller under `src/`. Only tests call it. `RunObserver._confirm` (`src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:276`) instead sets `tracked.confirmed = True` on the `TrackedLaunch` directly. That gives two ways to confirm a launch, and the tested one is not the one production uses. Tests that call `tracker.confirm` therefore don't exercise the real confirmation path. Route `_confirm` through `LaunchTracker.confirm` and keep the `_overdue` bookkeeping there, or drop the method and make the tests mutate state the way production does.

findings.title: `_close_recovered` can close an `unexpected_fault` escalation after one clean tick
findings.description: `_close_recovered` closes every open project escalation whose `fault_kind` is not in this tick's `TickFaults.kinds()`. `unexpected_fault` is written by `escalate()` in `faults.py`. It goes straight to `store.raise_project_escalation`, never through `TickFaults`, so it is never in the recurring set. The next tick that completes without cut-off therefore closes it. That includes the case where the node had a run in flight and `escalate` deliberately took the project-scoped path instead of blocking the node. A real, intermittent planner or decide bug would open and close an escalation within seconds, and no human gets a durable signal. If that is intended, say so in the `_close_recovered` docstring. If not, close only kinds the tick can re-observe (`run_observation_failed`, `launch_overdue`, `cf_probe_failed`) and leave `unexpected_fault` for a human to close. The store docstring says the `fault_kind` vocabulary is the Runner's. That makes an explicit allowlist cheap and safe against other writers later.

findings.title: Run-id and parameter validation is duplicated in three places
findings.description: The "entry has an unusable run id" check exists in `finish._run_id`, in `RunObserver._observe_one` (`observe.py:127-129`) and, as `_text_parameter`, in `launch.py`. They have the same failure shape but slightly different rules (the observer also rejects an empty string). The project guidelines require DRY. Extract one `run_id_of(entry)` helper next to `PARAM_RUN_ID` use, probably in `launch.py`, and have `finish` and `observe` call it. Then the rule can't drift between modules.

findings.title: Weakly typed test entry point relies on `type: ignore`
findings.description: `_hooked` returns `tuple[object, object]`. `main` then passes both items with `# type: ignore[arg-type]`, and the `Popen` call carries another `# type: ignore[call-overload]`. The Python rules include `tests/` in strict pyright, so these suppressions hide real signature mismatches. Typing the return as `tuple[PopenFactory, Callable[[str], RunPoll]]` removes two of the ignores. `test_tenant.py` has a similar gap: `make_rig: Any` loses the `Rig` type, and each test re-annotates it.

findings.title: Line over 88 characters and a text-count guard test
findings.description: The `except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - ...` line is about 90 characters, over the 88 limit. E501 is in the required rule set, so shorten the trailing comment. The catch is correctly a documented process-boundary handler: it logs with `logger.exception` and escalates. `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` guards it by counting the literal text `except Exception` across `*.py`. That is brittle: a docstring or comment containing the phrase breaks it, and `except BaseException` would not be counted. An `ast`-based check, as `test_import_boundaries.py` already does, would be sturdier.

findings.title: `observe.py` is over the file-size guideline
findings.description: The file is about 326 lines against the ~300-line guideline. The confirmed and unconfirmed observation paths are cohesive enough to split cleanly: the launch-confirmation logic (`_unconfirmed`, `_check_line`, `_after_launch_poll`, `_still_overdue`) could move to its own module. Not blocking.

findings.title: Process-boundary error handling and fault isolation
findings.description: Store failures and `UpstreamShapeError` re-raise so the process exits and recovery takes over. Everything else is logged with `logger.exception`, escalated through `escalate()`, and the other projects still tick. The narrower `except OSError` handlers in `launch.py`, `observe.py` and `probes.py` each carry an inline justification and return an answer for the caller to record. Both crash-recovery and per-project isolation have tests.

findings.title: Launch and journal ordering, budget enforcement, and test coverage
findings.description: The command is journaled before `Popen`, and unusable parameters are rejected before journaling. `finish.record` writes block then resolve idempotently, which is shown by the kill-between-block-and-resolve test. `TickBudget` is checked before every poll, `cf` call and launch, and `test_budget_coverage.py` fails any call site that starts after the deadline. The import-boundary rules (10 and 11) are enforced mechanically. The SIGKILL scenarios use real processes and condition-based waits, and nothing in the tests touches a production database variable.
